title: SDK: typed API errors + better 429 handling; add trace context propagation helpers
author: Ibrahim Khan
body: Summary: This PR improves error typing across the TS SDK, makes rate-limit (429) behavior predictable and template-friendly, and adds small helpers for W3C trace context propagation (traceparent/tracestate/baggage) so quickstart templates can reliably join client spans with Redwood Console traces. Motivation: We’ve seen recurring confusion in templates and support tickets around (a) distinguishing 429 vs other failures, (b) surfacing Retry-After and request_id in a structured way, and (c) ensuring trace context survives proxies/load balancers when users implement their own fetch/headers wrappers (SUP-2949, SUP-2934). Changes: (1) Typed errors: Introduce a discriminated union for SDK errors with stable error classes and codes: RedwoodAPIError (HTTP non-2xx), RedwoodRateLimitError (HTTP 429 with parsed retryAfterMs), RedwoodAuthError (401/403), RedwoodValidationError (400/422), RedwoodTransportError (network/DNS/TLS), and RedwoodTimeoutError (AbortError/timeout). All errors include best-effort context: requestId (x-redwood-request-id echoed back by API), status, route, region, and rawResponseBody (truncated) for safe debugging. (2) 429 handling: Update retry logic to (a) treat 429 as retryable for non-streaming requests by default, (b) honor Retry-After (seconds or HTTP date) when present with a capped wait, and (c) apply jittered exponential backoff when Retry-After is missing. Retries stop early on auth/validation errors and do not attempt to replay streaming responses once any bytes have been delivered to the caller. We now throw RedwoodRateLimitError when retries are exhausted so callers/templates can handle it explicitly (e.g., surface a user-facing “try again” vs “internal error”). (3) Trace context propagation helpers: Add a small, dependency-light module that can inject W3C trace context into outbound headers without forcing an OpenTelemetry dependency. New helpers: traceparentFromSpanContext(spanContext), injectTraceContext(headers, { traceparent, tracestate, baggage }), and headersWithTraceContext(baseHeaders, opts). Templates can use OTel if present (spanContext from @opentelemetry/api) or pass through existing traceparent strings (e.g., from incoming requests). This aligns with the quickstart telemetry contract expectations for trace joinability and Console deep links. (4) Docs/tests: Add unit tests for Retry-After parsing, 429 retry behavior, and traceparent formatting. Update README snippets used by quickstarts to show structured error handling and header injection. Notes on behavior: Default retries remain conservative. For 429, default maxRetries is 2 (3 total attempts) for non-streaming calls; for streaming we only retry on connection failure before the first token/chunk is received. If users need higher retry counts, they must opt in via client options. We also clamp Retry-After waits to avoid long sleeps in interactive workloads. API: No public method removals. One new exported type guard isRetryableError(err) and new exports for trace context helpers. Existing error objects are still instances of Error, but now have stable fields and names to switch on. Example usage (templates): try { await client.chat.completions.create(...) } catch (err) { if (err instanceof RedwoodRateLimitError) { logger.warn({ retryAfterMs: err.retryAfterMs, requestId: err.requestId }, 'rate limited'); } throw err; } and for tracing: const headers = headersWithTraceContext({ 'x-request-id': req.id }, { spanContext }); Checklist: Added/updated unit tests; no new runtime dependencies; verified quickstarts can consume new helper APIs; validated error object fields are safe to log (no prompt contents; response body truncated).
commits: sdk(core): add typed error classes + discriminated union
sdk(retry): honor Retry-After for 429; jittered backoff fallback
sdk(streaming): avoid replay after first chunk; improve disconnect errors
sdk(obs): add trace context helpers (traceparent/baggage injection)
tests: Retry-After parsing + rate-limit retries + traceparent formatting
docs: update error-handling and tracing snippets for quickstarts
conversation: Monica Patel: Can we ensure users can switch on error types without relying on message parsing? Also please confirm we surface request_id reliably.

Ibrahim Khan: Yep—errors are now discriminated by class + code. requestId is captured from x-redwood-request-id when present and included on all HTTP-derived errors; added a test that simulates header echo.
Sean Gallagher: Please keep 429 retries conservative. We don’t want templates hammering the API or masking quota issues. Also streaming retries need to avoid partial replay.
Ibrahim Khan: Agreed—default maxRetries=2 for 429 (non-streaming only). Streaming retries only happen if disconnect occurs before first chunk. Added explicit guard + test coverage.
Logan Wright: Trace context helper looks good. One ask: accept a precomputed traceparent string too (for gateway passthrough), not only spanContext.

Ibrahim Khan: Done—injectTraceContext takes { traceparent, tracestate, baggage } directly; headersWithTraceContext accepts either spanContext or explicit strings. Also added validation to avoid emitting malformed traceparent.
Dana Lo: Quickstarts will use this. Can you add a minimal example snippet showing Express/Next propagation from incoming headers?
Ibrahim Khan: Added README snippet: read incoming traceparent/baggage and pass through via headersWithTraceContext. Quickstarts docs PR will reference it.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash into main by Monica Patel on 2026-01-24. Squash commit: 8f3c0d9
release_notes:
- TypeScript SDK now throws typed errors (incl. RedwoodRateLimitError) with structured fields (status, requestId, retryAfterMs).
- Improved default handling of HTTP 429 with Retry-After support and conservative retries.
- Added lightweight W3C trace context propagation helpers for quickstart templates (traceparent/tracestate/baggage).
